speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset lower back pain that radiates down your leg. To help me determine the cause, could you describe exactly where the pain travels in your leg and what activities make it worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That sounds like a sciatic nerve irritation. Does lifting your leg while lying flat cause pain, or is the pain present at rest? Also, do you feel any numbness or weakness in your foot?

REQUEST TEST: Neurological_examination (reflexes, sensation, motor strength)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Sensation: Intact to light touch and pin-prick throughout the leg and foot; Motor_Function: No significant weakness noted; Reflexes: Normal ankle and knee reflexes.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sharp lower back pain radiating to the leg and foot. I also have Pain worsens with movement, The onset of pain while exercising. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the history of sudden pain during exercise radiating to the foot, I need to assess for a disc herniation. Can you tell me if you feel any numbness or tingling in your leg, and did you hear a "pop" when the pain started?

REQUEST TEST: MRI_Lumbar_Spine

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Lumbar_Spine: Evidence of L5-S1 disc herniation impinging on the adjacent nerve root.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: L5-S1 Disc Herniation. The history of sudden pain during exercise radiating to the foot, combined with MRI findings of an L5-S1 disc herniation impinging on the nerve root, confirms this diagnosis.
